blocks.text: I can interpret scatter graphs.
You will learn how to spot correlation on a scatter graph, and what it does and does not tell us about the data.
Tap the word to see what it means.

items.def: Correlation describes the extent to which the relationship is close to a linear relationship.

blocks.text: Correlation may be positive or negative, depending on whether one variable generally increases as another increases, or whether it decreases.
Scatter graphs can be used to investigate the nature of a relationship between two variables.

If the points seem to form a discernible shape or pathway through the graph, that suggests the two variables are {associated}. If the points are all over the place, as if randomly placed, there is not much of an association.

blocks.label: Why does a pathway matter?
blocks.text: A pathway leaves some parts of the graph without any points. That suggests the variables are interacting with each other in some way.
An association may be linear or non-linear.

items.title: {Linear}
items.sub: the points form a straight line

blocks.text: When the points appear to form a straight line, the rate of change is constant throughout the data. In these cases, there is correlation.
When the points form a curve, there is a relationship between the variables. But {correlation} is not the best model for this association.
When the points form an **upward sloping line**, we describe the variables as having {positive correlation}.
Each time the independent variable increases, the dependent variable increases at a constant rate.
When the points form a **downward sloping line**, we describe the variables as having {negative correlation}.
Each time the independent variable increases, the dependent variable decreases at a constant rate.

blocks.q: Which type of relationship does each description of a scatter graph show?

items.text: The points follow a straight line sloping upwards
As one variable increases, the other increases at a constant rate
The points follow a straight line sloping downwards
As one variable increases, the other decreases at a constant rate
The points seem to be randomly placed all over the graph

blocks.text: Correlation can be clearer to see in some scatter graphs than in others. Two graphs can both show positive correlation, but in one the relationship between the variables is clearer.
The clearer graph is the one where the points are more {tightly packed} along the pathway of a straight line.

blocks.q: Graph A and Graph B both show positive correlation. In Graph A the points are tightly packed along a straight line. In Graph B the points are more spread out. Which graph shows the clearer correlation?
options: They are exactly as clear as each other
blocks.why: The clearer correlation is where the points are more tightly packed along the straight-line pathway.

blocks.text: A small amount of data may not be enough to make a reliable assessment of correlation.

Andeep plotted sunshine and temperature for Bradford for just five months. The points sloped downwards, so it looked like negative correlation: months with more sunshine tend to be colder. But that doesn’t seem right.

blocks.label: What happened with more data?
blocks.text: With every month from 1941 to 2022, it now looks like a positive correlation: months with more sunshine tend to be warmer. That makes more sense. The five points may just have been a chance finding.
A more accurate assessment of correlation can be obtained by plotting a {larger amount} of data points.
A correlation tells us how the variables tend to change, so we should describe it in the context of the data.
Stornoway weather data (every month from 1941 to 2022) can be modelled with a negative correlation between rainfall and sunshine.

blocks.label: What does that suggest?
blocks.text: The more rainfall there is in a month, the less visible sunshine there is likely to be.

blocks.q: Choose the statement that best describes what each correlation suggests.

items.q: Suppose a scatter graph of the temperature and the number of ice creams sold each day shows positive correlation.
options: On hotter days, more ice creams tend to be sold
On hotter days, fewer ice creams tend to be sold

items.q: Suppose a scatter graph of the temperature and the number of hot drinks sold each day shows negative correlation.
options: On hotter days, more hot drinks tend to be sold
On hotter days, fewer hot drinks tend to be sold
The points must form a curve

blocks.text: A scatter graph of regions in England and Wales shows a positive correlation between the number of cell phone towers and transport emissions. Does that mean cell towers cause transport emissions?
That doesn’t seem likely. Building more cell towers is unlikely to directly cause more transport emissions.

items.title: Population goes up
items.sub: more cell towers are likely to be built

blocks.text: Both variables have a positive correlation with {population}. That can explain the positive correlation between cell towers and transport emissions.

blocks.q: Two variables show positive correlation on a scatter graph. Which conclusion is the safest?
options: One variable definitely causes the other to increase
The variables tend to increase together, but this does not prove one causes the other
There is no association between the variables
blocks.why: A positive correlation does not always mean that an increase in one variable is causing an increase in the other. Both might depend on a third variable.

blocks.text: Aisha, Jacob and Sam have data about jobs in 2023: mean hours worked per week and mean weekly pay. Each has a different idea about the correlation.

items: Aisha: working more hours per week means you earn more, so positive correlation.
Jacob: some jobs pay more than others, so no correlation.
Sam: if your job pays more you can afford to work fewer hours, so negative correlation.

blocks.label: What does the scatter graph show?
blocks.text: Overall, there seems to be a positive correlation. Most of the points form an upward sloping straight line, but some points don’t quite fit.

items: The distribution of the points may suggest correlation, which can be positive or negative, or suggest there is no correlation or association.
Points forming a straight line suggest correlation. Points forming a curve show a non-linear association.
Correlation is easier to assess when there is a larger amount of data.
Interpret the correlation in the context of the data.
Correlation does not necessarily mean that one variable is affecting the other.

flashcards.back: The extent to which the relationship between two variables is close to a linear relationship.

flashcards.front: What shape of points suggests positive correlation?
What shape of points suggests negative correlation?
What does it mean if the points on a scatter graph seem randomly placed all over the graph?
flashcards.back: There is not much of an association between the two variables.

flashcards.front: If the points form a curve, is correlation the best model?
flashcards.back: No. There is a non-linear association, but correlation is not the best model for it.

flashcards.front: Two scatter graphs both show positive correlation. In which is the correlation clearer?
flashcards.back: The one where the points are more tightly packed along a straight line.

flashcards.front: Why is a small amount of data a problem when assessing correlation?
flashcards.back: It may not be enough for a reliable assessment. A larger amount of data gives a more accurate assessment.

flashcards.front: Rainfall and sunshine in Stornoway show negative correlation. What does that suggest?
flashcards.back: The more rainfall there is in a month, the less visible sunshine there is likely to be.

flashcards.front: Does correlation always mean that one variable causes the other?
flashcards.back: No. Two variables may be correlated because they both depend on a third variable.

flashcards.front: Cell towers and transport emissions are positively correlated. Which third variable is linked to both?
flashcards.back: Population. As population increases, both the number of cell towers and the transport emissions tend to increase.

flashcards.front: When points form a straight line, what does that suggest about the rate of change?
flashcards.back: It is constant throughout the data.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Checking understanding of correlation
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with one word or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: What word describes the extent to which the relationship between two variables is close to a linear relationship?
questions.explanation: Correlation describes how close the relationship is to a linear relationship.

questions.prompt: The points on a scatter graph form an upward sloping straight line. Is the correlation positive or negative?
questions.explanation: An upward sloping line means that as one variable increases, the other increases too.

questions.prompt: The points on a scatter graph form a downward sloping straight line. Is the correlation positive or negative?
questions.explanation: A downward sloping line means that as one variable increases, the other decreases.

questions.prompt: The points on a scatter graph form a curve. Is correlation the best model for this association? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: A curve shows a non-linear association, and correlation is not the best model for it.

questions.prompt: The points on a scatter graph seem to be randomly placed all over the graph. Is there an association between the variables? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Randomly placed points do not form a shape or pathway, so there is not much of an association.

questions.prompt: A more accurate assessment of correlation can be obtained by plotting a (smaller or larger) amount of data. Which word is correct?
questions.explanation: A small amount of data may not be enough for a reliable assessment; more data points give a more accurate one.

questions.prompt: Stornoway rainfall and sunshine show a negative correlation. As the rainfall in a month increases, does the sunshine tend to increase or decrease?
questions.explanation: Negative correlation means one variable decreases as the other increases: more rainfall means less visible sunshine.

questions.prompt: Cell towers and transport emissions in a region are both positively correlated with which third variable? Give one word.
questions.explanation: As the population of a region increases, both cell towers and transport emissions tend to increase.

questions.prompt: A pupil says that a correlation between two variables always shows that one causes the other. Is the pupil right? Answer yes or no.
questions.explanation: Correlation does not necessarily imply that one variable is affecting the other.
